# orca recovery

Every `orca recovery` command. Ids: a full id, a unique prefix, or (projects) a name or path.

## `orca recovery list [--all]`

what blocks dispatch: global, group and run blockers, tasks held for a person, and runs a stop could not end

- What it does: reads from the panel (no write).
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `--all`: also list the handoff rows whose request is finished

## `orca recovery retry [--run <run>] [--group <group>] [--acknowledge <acknowledge>]`

resume a run (--run) or a group (--group) blocked for a reason other than a terminal failure

- What it does: sends control verb `recovery-retry`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `--run <run>`: a blocked run
- `--group <group>`: a blocked group
- `--acknowledge <acknowledge>`: charge-remaining-grant|charge-observed-floor: settle a single call's unknown usage (a requirement, estimate or flow call) by charging its remaining grant, then retry (--run only; an agent may send it without a person token, tester follow-up E §8; a requirement or estimate call's charge above 250,000 tokens needs one (C-1); refused to a run Orca dispatched); charge-observed-floor charges instead the floor ccloop observed, marked approximate (a requirement or estimate call with a finite remainder and a known floor; never a flow call)
